subject: Regional custody options for short-window analytics hops — operational and subprocessor asks
messages:
From: Will Harris <will.harris@saffron-analytics.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: dpo@saffron-analytics.com, procurement@saffron-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 17:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Quick question on short-window cross-border hops for analytics

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have one operational/legal question that came up in our DPA review: our analytics pipeline collects anonymized user event blobs in the EU but we sometimes allow a 24-48 hour analytics processing hop to the US for heavy aggregation/ML jobs, and an occasional fallback to APAC for cost/latency reasons during outages. Our DPO wants to understand how Redwood treats custody in those short-window hops and specifically: 1) whether you consider that "transfer" under our DPA language, 2) what subprocessors would be involved in the US/APAC hops, and 3) whether we can get an addendum that commits to region-pinning for primary processing and documents the conditional short-window exceptions.

Can you point me at the operational guarantees you can provide (e.g., max hop duration, telemetry/audit evidence we can expect), and any template addendum you use? Procurement will need the high level for contract review.

Appreciate a quick pointer — we are aiming to finalize the contract next week.

Best,
Will
DPO (for Saffron Analytics)

[No attachments]

From: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Will Harris <will.harris@saffron-analytics.com>
Cc: dpo@saffron-analytics.com, procurement@saffron-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 00:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on short-window cross-border hops for analytics

Hi Will —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: 1) We treat the short-window hop as processing that may be considered a transfer under most DPAs unless explicitly scoped as an operational exception; we can document a conditional exception in a DPA addendum, 2) subprocessors depend on routing (hosted vs dedicated) but typically include our analytics/telemetry processor (US) and a cloud edge cache (APAC), and 3) yes — we have an addendum template that enumerates primary-region pinning + permitted short-window conditions, telemetry evidence, and timeline commitments.

I've attached a draft Redwood DPA addendum (redline-friendly) and the current subprocessor roster for the services that touch logs/telemetry. Highlights to call out:
- Primary processing can be pinned to EU for the customer-controlled model when you select EU residency.
- We allow transient hops for operational reasons with configurable max windows (default 72 hours) — we can tighten to 24/48 for Saffron in the addendum.
- Telemetry: we can provide per-request region stamp and a daily condensed audit extract for the hops; full request-level logs can be made available under an escrow/ops request.
- Subprocessor visibility: the roster lists which vendors are engaged in each region; we can provide SLA-backed substitution guarantees for the analytics pipeline in the addendum.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm desired maximum transient window (24 or 48 hours), 2) we loop Karthik for the operational checklist, and 3) our legal team will prepare a redline-ready addendum.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow with our DPA lead and infra ops.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_2026-01.csv

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Will Harris <will.harris@saffron-analytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 09:15:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: Quick question on short-window cross-border hops for analytics

Will / Marissa —

Quick operational context from infra:
- For Hosted API customers with EU pinning, primary inference and telemetry storage are pinned to our EU region by default.
- Short-window hops occur when batch analytics jobs are routed to dedicated US compute for cost/throughput or to APAC when EU capacity is constrained.
- We instrument each token/request with a region stamp and retain a hopping trace. We can produce a daily CSV extract that shows request_id, timestamp_utc, origin_region, hopped_to_region, hop_duration_seconds.

Two specific asks for Saffron to decide:
1) Desired hard hop ceiling (we can set 24h or 48h; below 24h requires additional ops controls),
2) Whether you want the daily condensed audit only or request-level traces on-demand (the latter requires an ops escalation and a narrow support SLA).

Operationally, for a 24h ceiling we will also:
- Lock cache eviction policies for your keys to favor EU-prefetching,
- Disable APAC fallback for analytics unless EU capacity is fully saturated AND you pre-authorize the fallback window,
- Add a monitoring alert (pager/Slack) to your on-call to notify on any forced hop.

I can produce a short ops-runbook (playbook) that maps the conditions and the exact telemetry fields.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[No attachments in this message]

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: will.harris@saffron-analytics.com, dpo@saffron-analytics.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 11:47:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on short-window cross-border hops for analytics

Hi all —

Legal takeaways for the addendum we should align on before we send over a redline:
1) Definitive primary-region commitment (EU) and a short-window carveout clause that lists explicit triggers (capacity, emergency ops, lawful orders).
2) Maximum hop duration: we will state a default (72h) but insert customer-specific ceiling (24/48) as negotiated. For Saffron we should offer the 24h ceiling with an escalation path to request temporary extension (documented and timeboxed).
3) Audit evidence and retention: we will provide daily condensed audit extracts for the last 90 days; request-level traces are available for 180 days under an elevated support agreement.
4) Subprocessor controls: include a commitment to notify customers 30 days before adding new subprocessors that could handle hopped data, and a right to request substitution where a viable alternative exists.

Marissa — please confirm Saffron's preference on the two choices Karthik listed (24h vs 48h, condensed audit vs request-level on demand) and whether procurement needs any extra procurement-friendly language (e.g., SLA credits for unauthorized hops). Once we have that I will draft the redline and route to our legal ops.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Will Harris <will.harris@saffron-analytics.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: dpo@saffron-analytics.com, procurement@saffron-analytics.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 16:23:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on short-window cross-border hops for analytics

Hi Laura / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. Saffron is comfortable with the following:
- 24-hour hard ceiling for transient hops (we want the stricter setting),
- Daily condensed audit extract as the baseline; request-level traces only on-demand under an elevated support SLA,
- 30-day notification for new subprocessors and the right to request substitution,
- We do not need SLA credits for unauthorized hops at contract start but would like a clause to revisit credits if unauthorized hops occur more than twice in a 90-day rolling window.

Please proceed with the redline and we can plan a 30-minute legal/ops sync tomorrow at 09:00 CET to finalize. Procurement will attach the PO once the addendum is agreed.

Best,
Will Harris
Head of Data Governance | Saffron Analytics
